target_customer: Robotics and hardware companies that need small-batch contract manufacturing in the US (customers named on its site include university labs, the ISS National Lab and robot makers)
problem: Hardware startups depend on slow overseas sourcing and manual contract manufacturers for prototypes and low-volume builds. Tensr wants autonomous robotic factory cells that take on-demand orders and ship within 24 hours.
business_model: Contract manufacturing services priced per order, built on robotic factory cells (SMT, machining, additive, injection molding, assembly)

founders.name: Eric Berndt
education: UC Berkeley, MS and BS in EE/CS (YC launch page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he raced autonomous full-scale IndyCars at 160 mph as a Berkeley robotics researcher. Individual prior employers are not stated.

founders.name: Adith Sundram
education: UC Berkeley, MS and BS in ME (YC launch page)
founders.background_notes: Robotics, ML and controls work at UC Berkeley per the YC page.

founders.name: C.K. Wolfe
prior_employers: UC Berkeley robotics lab under BAIR (technical program manager)
education: UC Berkeley, PhD in CS (AI, Robotics)
founders.background_notes: YC page credits him with raising 17M USD or more in DARPA and industry sponsorship for a Berkeley and Stanford racing team in 2024.

technical_complexity.rationale: Running a multi-process factory (SMT line, machining, additive, molding) with autonomous cells and software that schedules orders is hardware heavy, even though the team is Berkeley robotics researchers with an autonomous racing background.

defensibility.rationale: The pitch is a data and process loop where orders become training data, but contract manufacturing is capital intensive and replicable by better funded rivals. Nothing in the sources shows a lock-in yet.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet observable. Automated factory startups such as Foundry Robotics raised large rounds in 2026, after Tensr's launch.

market_need_then: The YC launch page frames the status quo as overseas sourcing from China with long lead times. Customers named on the company site include robot makers and the ISS National Lab, but no demand metrics are published.

branding.domain_note: Company uses tensr.com, an exact match with a vowel dropped from the word tensor.

identity.logo: Logo image on the YC page; no source describes it
identity.voice_and_tone: Ambitious infrastructure framing such as the AWS of manufacturing and the physical equivalent of cloud compute

brand_strength.rationale: Very early. Coverage so far is one launch article and aggregator pages; no source shows community or press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: Tensr is an active early stage company with a small team and a physical factory in Emeryville. It has no exit and no verified funding rounds in public sources, so the outcome is still open. The key risks are capital intensity and whether customer orders turn into the data loop the founders describe.
notes: Unverified: VCBacked and PitchBook list 500K USD raised, pre-seed, December 2025, investor Y Combinator; no outlet or company source confirms it, so it is not recorded as a round. Batch conflict: the CSV says Summer 2026 and the YC page agrees, but the YC launch post is about a year old and several aggregators say Fall 2025. Competitor sources found (Bright Machines, Formic, Foundry Robotics) were not dated near founding, so the list is empty. Founder prior employers beyond team level claims (Rockwell Automation, aerospace, medical devices) are not attributed to individuals. Searches for outcome events and name origin found nothing. Completeness pass: the $500K pre-seed rests on aggregators only (VCBacked, FundedIQ); StartupHub shows an unrelated $4M figure that looks like a different company and is not recorded.
